_doc: v79.15.0 (item 1): the verified analysis step's tables and prompt (src/rag/analysis_step.py, flag ANALYSIS_STEP). One model call (thinking off, temperature 0, a JSON reply, as the fit) between the frame and rendering decides the leading and subordinate lines and every schema element's esito, each claim citing ids the code verifies: S-ids (the case's sentences as issue_records.sentences numbers them, the system's assumptions left out) and A-ids (the fitted norms' texts as their numbered periods: applicability.article_ids). deadline_s: the step's wall-clock budget, the re-ask included (a call not back by then: nothing from the step); max_tokens: the reply's budget per call; max_article_chars: an article's periods in the prompt are cut there (logged; verification always reads every period). esiti: the element verdicts. assertion_verbs: the verbs (regular expressions, matched as whole words, case-insensitive) after which a sentence's grammatical subject is the one asserting it -- a non-client party of the verified frame or an authority (authority_words) asserting it makes the sentence a reported assertion, never proof. authority_words: the accusing authorities (accusa, Procura, PM, investigatori -- the brief's -- and their other spellings). speaker_prefixes: the words a sentence names its speaker after («Secondo la società, …»); speaker_prefixes_initial: the same, read only at the sentence's start or after a comma, semicolon or colon («Per la Procura, …» -- «per» anywhere else is no speaker). A passive's agent after an assertion verb's participle («è accusato da Giulia Neri») is a speaker too. A sentence is a reported assertion when any of its asserting phrases names a non-client party or an authority as the one speaking, whatever the client says in the same sentence. labels: the prompt's section titles. remedy_mark: how a fitted norm of the remedy set (data/remedy_articles.json) is marked in the prompt. reask: the one re-ask's message, {reasons} the rejection reasons, one per line. prompt_system: the system prompt (joined with newlines), hashed (prompt_hash) and logged with every run. qa_statements (build B, rendering with the flag on): how a prose sentence of «Risposte ai quesiti» is read as a statement of what a norm provides -- it cites an article (citations.article_refs) and holds one of «verbs» (regular expressions, whole words, any case) -- and matched to a verified affermazione_di_diritto: the same article number and at least «overlap» of the sentence's tokens (words of «token_min_len» letters or more, lowercased, «stopwords» out) in the statement's tokens (the denominator: the sentence's tokens). A sentence with no verified counterpart is removed (qa_sentences_dropped, logged). «verbs» holds the rule's phrasings too (deve, è tenuto, la pena, reclusione, …); referents: the words a sentence names a norm by without its number («la norma», «la disposizione», …) -- such a sentence with one of the verbs is a statement on whichever article, matched against every verified statement. law_statements.overlap: an affermazione_di_diritto is kept only when at least this share of its tokens (the same tokens) is in the text of the periods it cites, and every article it names has one of its own periods among them. v79.15.1: the schema elements go to the model as ids, «- [A<articolo>:E<n>] <testo>» under labels.elements (the A-ids' article token), and the reply cites them in elemento_in_gioco and elementi[].elemento -- verified by existence only. reask: «{allowed}» the articles a line may stand on (the fitted norms not in the remedy set) with their E-ids, «{claimant}» the line «reask_claimant» when the client brings the claim (dropped otherwise). claimant: «roles» the verified frame's ruolo values (valore or intake) that make the client the claimant, «defendant_roles» those that never do, «party_words» the words of the client party's ruolo_nel_fatto that make him the claimant when no role decides. exception: what makes a schema element an exception or a limit, never a claimant's line -- «schema_kinds» (element_schemas kinds) and «special_kinds» (a comma speciale's kind) when the element carries its schema kind; else «keywords» (regular expressions, accent- and case-folded, matched from a word's start) on the element's text and on the words before it in its clause of the article. v79.15.1 (item 4) prose_review: the Q&A, §4's prose and §7's model-written objections and answers reviewed sentence by sentence (analysis_step.ProseReview) -- a statement of what a norm provides with no verified counterpart is replaced by the first verified affermazione_di_diritto on the same article, verbatim; with none it is dropped, and so is the next sentence when it opens with one of «anaphoric_openers» (accent- and case-folded, a whole-word prefix: the brief's list -- Inoltre, Pertanto, Ai sensi del primo / secondo / medesimo, Tale, Questo/a, Essa/Esso, In particolare, Infatti, Tuttavia), and the one after that likewise while each opens so; a sentence citing an article the binding excluded or the fit removed is dropped; one citing an article outside the fitted set (the analysis input's norms, the remedies §4 names) that the user did not name is dropped -- an article of «exempt_codes» (applicability.article_key's code: the procedural codes, whose articles the fit never judges) never counts as outside. v79.15.1 (review) prose_review.bare_article: an article cited by number alone («l'art. 1439», «gli artt. 1439 e 1440») -- a number the shared parser does not read -- is read by the review too (bare_cited), resolved by its number among the fitted, the named and the excluded articles (else an article outside the fitted set): «suffixes» the number's latin suffixes, «comma_ordinals» a comma clause skipped after the number («, secondo comma,»), «source_words» (regular expressions, any case) the words after the number that tie it to a named source (del, della, c., cost., legge, …) -- such a citation is never read as a bare number. v79.15.2 (hotfix) article_key: every article comparison of the step goes through one canonical key (analysis_step.art_key: the number with its suffix and the code, lower-case, no space or punctuation -- «640 c.p.», «art. 640 c.p.», «Art. 640 cp», «640cp», «A640cp» are «640cp»; «62-bis c.p.» is «62biscp»; «640 c.p.p.» is «640cpp», another article): the reply's articolo, the E-ids' prefix, the remedy set, the fitted set, the frame's charge, the user-named articles, the re-ask's allowed list, the objections, the law statements; «codes» maps a code's compact spelling (its document name or a long abbreviation, punctuation and spaces out) to its key; «law_prefixes» maps a law's spelled-out kind before its number to its sigla («legge n. 241/1990» and «L. n. 241/1990» are both «l2411990»; a law's own number always kept, so two laws of one year stay apart). A period id («A640cp.1») is read as its article; «640 del codice penale» as «640cp». The displayed and logged articolo stays the fitted norm's label. analysis_fallback_skipped_reason: why the rubrica fallback did not run, a string in block_counters and the analysis_step line -- line_verified, frame_charge_used, no_named_charge, no_rubrica_match, step_failed, no_input; "" when it ran. v79.17.1 (item 9) rito_codes: the frame's rito -> the codes of its family (article_key keys: cp, cpp for the penal riti; cc, cpc for the civil ones). An article of a code in this table but outside the frame's rito (1439 c.c. in a penal case) is never the leading line and is a subordinate line only when the fit tagged it as governing the pretesa or a quesito; otherwise context (analysis_step.outside_rito, counter analysis_line_outside_rito_rejected). A rito not in the table, no verified rito, a special law or a code not in the table: nothing restricted. v79.18.0 (A1-A2, items 10-13): the binding's set carries its tiers (interactive_flow.binding_pretesa «tiers»: si_verificato > dipende_verificato > non_verificato; the unverified «si» / «dipende» are in the set, untrusted), read into the input's «binding.tiers»; a model line that fails twice with a non-empty set leads with the set's best-tier article (analysis_step.set_fallback, stato insieme_governante, every element da_provare, analysis_line_fallback_set, fallback reason set_line_used) -- never «da determinare» with a non-empty set; the honesty line only on an empty set. degree_words: item 11 (above). An element carries its comma (the record's requisite's) for the strategy step's claimant forza (item 10). A record fact the client stated («chi» the client) is certo in §2, never an allegation, and the client is never the party «che afferma» of a contestato (item 13). v79.18.1 (C7): the accusing authority's charge sentence is a «contestazione dell'accusa», never an «allegazione» -- §2's label, the table's esito (analysis_step.CONTESTED_BY_ACCUSA), §10's question, §7's objection (rendering.obiezioni.contestazione_accusa); the frame's unverified fields are logged, not printed in §10. v79.18.5 (item 6): general_part_links -- a general-part article's concept words; a ruling on it is kept in §5 when a word is in an element of the line (analysis_step.general_part_attached), the C8 filter applying to the unattached ones only.

labels.line_rank: Preferenza per la linea (prima il fit si verificato, poi dipende verificato, poi non verificato)

remedy_mark: rimedio o parte generale: mai una linea
reask: La risposta precedente è stata respinta per questi motivi:
Articoli ammessi come linea (A<articolo>) con gli id dei loro elementi:
Correggi e rispondi di nuovo SOLO con l'oggetto JSON completo.
reask_claimant: Il cliente agisce come attore: l'elemento in gioco è uno degli elementi costitutivi elencati, mai un'eccezione o un limite.

claimant._doc: v79.15.3 (item 2): the client's side from the verified frame only (analysis_step.client_side). Each entry is a whole word or phrase, accent- and case-folded. First the verified ruolo (valore and intake, a «/» or «_» read as a space): a word of «roles» -> claimant, of «defendant_roles» -> defence. Else the verified ruolo_nel_fatto of the client's party (frame.parti, lato «cliente» or the client's name): only «roles» words -> claimant, only «defendant_roles» words -> defence, both or none -> neither. «worker»: its words count as a claimant's only when the verified rito is one of «riti» and the frame verifies an addebito_o_domanda (the claim is the worker's); otherwise they are no side word. No verified role -> neither (claimant False, as before). The brief's sets; the feminine and plural forms added (several clients: «committenti», «indagati»); locatore and conduttore both claimant (the brief lists both). v79.18.4: the persona offesa (parte offesa, parte civile; the frame's ruolo «persona_offesa») is a claimant: the victim's side rules, never the defence's -- 79.18.2's pretesa-tipo fallback (accusa -> difesa) no longer reaches her.

rendering._doc: v79.15.3 (items 1, 3): the texts the code prints from the verified analysis (user-visible, docs/copy_review.md). tesi: a verified linea_principale / linea_subordinata's printed sentence, by the client's side (analysis_step.client_side: difesa | attore | neutro) and the verified esito of its elemento_in_gioco; {elemento} the schema's text of the line's E-id, {art} the line's article, {fatti} the element verdict's cited sentences no other party asserts (reported_by: a counterparty's allegation never stands as the fact that proves or excludes; none: the line's own such sentences), each «as written» without its final stop, joined by «fatti_sep»; none: «nessun_fatto». The model's tesi is logged only (tesi_modello). obiezioni: §7's entries from the verified analysis, one form for all: the allegation's sentence as written («allegazione»; «allegazione_attribuita» when the sentence itself names no speaker) or the exception element («eccezione»), answered by the status of each element in words («stato», by side; «stato_attore» for a claimant) joined by «stati_sep», then «: » and the client's own cited sentences («risposta_con_fatti»), none: «risposta_senza_fatti».

prompt_system: Sei un avvocato italiano. Ricevi il quadro verificato del caso, i fatti numerati (S1, S2, …), le norme ritenute applicabili con gli elementi del loro schema numerati (A<articolo>:E<n>) e il loro testo diviso in periodi numerati (A<articolo>.<n>), e i quesiti dell'utente. Decidi la linea e l'esito di ogni elemento. Ogni affermazione cita gli id su cui si fonda: il codice verifica ogni id e scarta ciò che non è citato o non esiste.

- "linea_principale": {"articolo": l'articolo come ti è dato, "elemento_in_gioco": l'id di un elemento del suo schema (A<articolo>:E<n>), "tesi": UNA sola frase, "cita_fatti": [id dei fatti], "cita_norma": [id dei periodi di quell'articolo]};

- "elementi": per l'articolo della linea principale e per quello della subordinata, per ogni elemento del suo schema: {"articolo": l'articolo, "elemento": l'id dell'elemento (A<articolo>:E<n>), "esito": "provato" | "contestato" | "da_provare" | "escluso", "cita_fatti": [id dei fatti], "parte_che_afferma": il nome di una parte del quadro, oppure null};
- "affermazioni_di_diritto": per ogni affermazione su ciò che una norma prevede: {"testo": UNA sola frase, "cita_norma": [id dei periodi]}.
- La linea è l'articolo su cui il caso si decide. L'addebito o la domanda del quadro, quando c'è, è la linea principale o la subordinata.
- Un articolo segnato «rimedio o parte generale» non è mai una linea.
- Se il cliente è attore o ricorrente, l'elemento in gioco è un elemento costitutivo della sua domanda, mai un'eccezione, un limite o un termine di decadenza che la controparte può opporgli.

- "provato" solo se un fatto citato lo dimostra. Ciò che una parte diversa dal cliente afferma, sostiene, dichiara o contesta (anche l'accusa, la Procura, il PM, gli investigatori) non prova nulla: l'elemento è "contestato" e "parte_che_afferma" è quella parte.
- "escluso" solo se un fatto citato lo esclude; "da_provare" se nessun fatto lo decide.
- Le dichiarazioni del cliente contro se stesso valgono come fatti.
- Usa solo gli id dati. Non citare altre norme né la giurisprudenza.
Rispondi SOLO con un oggetto JSON, senza testo prima o dopo:

objection_answer_check._doc: v79.15.3 (item 3): a §7 answer sentence (the plan's / model's objections kept after the verified ones; ProseReview with site «obiezioni», the answer) asserts an element as integrato / provato -- read clause by clause (analysis_step.asserted_unproven): «affirmations» taken out first (emphatic phrases, no negation); periods cut at «;», at «:» before a space and at «period_breaks», clauses at «,»; a period holding one of «attributions» reports another party's claim and asserts nothing; a clause asserts when it holds one of «verbs» (whole words from their start, any case) with none of «negations» BEFORE that verb in the same clause (a negation, a modal or conditional marker -- explicit word forms: «va provato», «deve essere provato», «resta da provare», «se fosse provato» assert nothing; «restituzione», «contesto», «il difetto» negate nothing); the element is the one the clause names -- its E-id («A640cp:E1»), «E<n>» or «elemento <n>» of a line article, its schema text folded, or at least «overlap» of the element's tokens (the Q&A's tokens(): words of 3+ letters, stopwords out; the denominator the element's) -- else the one a preceding verbless clause of the same period names. The element named best (id or text first, then the highest overlap; a tie with a «provato» or «escluso» one keeps the clause) held «da_provare» or «contestato» by the verified table -> the sentence dropped (objections_sentences_dropped, motivo «elemento_non_provato»), its anaphoric follower with it.

degree_words._doc: v79.18.0 (item 11): the degree words of the schema texts, by grade (a higher grade is a stronger degree). An element holding one (its highest grade) is «provato» only when a cited fact holds a word of the same or a higher grade; else the code sets «da_provare» (analysis_step.degree_grade, counter analysis_degree_downgraded, logged «degree_downgraded»). Patterns: regular expressions on the accent- and case-folded text.
